title: Flasque cosimplicial Godement resolutions with pointwise multiplication
statement: For a scheme X and module sheaves F,G, there exist cosimplicial module sheaves A,B,C, quasi-isomorphic augmentations of the zero extensions of their alternating coface complexes from F[0],G[0],(F tensor G)[0], and a natural pointwise tensor multiplication A tensor B to C agreeing with tensor sections in degree zero. All terms of the extended complexes are flasque. No cochain map on the total tensor complex is asserted.

source.place: Section 20.30, Lemma 20.30.1 (0FKS); pointwise multiplication: Banerjee, arXiv:1004.1491, §1.1.4, pp. 15–16.

proof.text: Apply moduleCup_godement_model_pairing to construct the three augmented concrete Godement models and their compatible pointwise multiplication.
Apply moduleCup_godement_model_quasiIso to each of F, G and F tensor G. The model predicate supplies the actual Godement cofaces and germ maps, so all three augmentations are quasi-isomorphisms.

For a nonnegative integer n, use extendXIso and the model term equality to identify the complex term with T(T^n(F)), and transport flasqueness along this isomorphism using naturality of the sheaf restriction maps. Apply moduleCup_godement_object_flasque. For negative n, extension by zero gives a zero object; evaluation carries it to zero groups and every restriction between zero groups is an isomorphism, hence epi. Repeat for G and F tensor G.

Assemble the three quasi-isomorphisms, the three flasqueness families, and the degree-zero pairing identity from the construction theorem into the original existential conjunction, with all statements and definitions unchanged.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 20.30.1 plus the monoidal Godement construction in Banerjee section 1.1.4; explicit flasqueness transport compiled in Lean

lean.statement:
theorem moduleCup_godement_cosimplicial_input (X : Scheme.{u}) (F G : X.Modules) :
    ∃ (A B C : CosimplicialObject X.Modules)
      (a : (CochainComplex.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F ⟶
        moduleCup_cosimplicialComplex X A)
      (b : (CochainComplex.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj G ⟶
        moduleCup_cosimplicialComplex X B)
      (c : (CochainComplex.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj (F ⊗ G) ⟶
        moduleCup_cosimplicialComplex X C)
      (μ : moduleCup_cosimplicialTensor X A B ⟶ C),
      QuasiIso a ∧ QuasiIso b ∧ QuasiIso c ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, TopCat.Sheaf.IsFlasque
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)).obj
          ((moduleCup_cosimplicialComplex X A).X n))) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, TopCat.Sheaf.IsFlasque
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)).obj
          ((moduleCup_cosimplicialComplex X B).X n))) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, TopCat.Sheaf.IsFlasque
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)).obj
          ((moduleCup_cosimplicialComplex X C).X n))) ∧
      ∀ (V : X.Opens)
        (x : Γ(((CochainComplex.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F).X 0, V))
        (y : Γ(((CochainComplex.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj G).X 0, V)),
        (moduleCup_cosimplicialZeroPair X A B C μ).val.app (op V)
          (tmulSection ((a.f 0).val.app (op V) x) ((b.f 0).val.app (op V) y)) =
        (c.f 0).val.app (op V) (tmulSection x y)
